\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Simulation under the null that the wage bill has no effect on growth. Observed GDP, growth and controls are kept and only the wage bill ratio s = W/Y is replaced by a synthetic series. A (main): ln s\_sim,t = ln s\_obs,t$-$1 $-$ (1 $-$ ε) Δln Y\_t + u\_t, with Δln Y the observed growth of nominal GDP and u drawn with replacement from the country's own values of Δln s\_obs + (1 $-$ ε) Δln Y, recentred to zero within country. B: ln s\_sim,t = μ\_i + ρ (ln s\_sim,t$-$1 $-$ μ\_i) $-$ (1 $-$ ε) Δln Y\_t + u\_t, with ρ = 0.870 (within-country AR(1) of the observed log ratio), μ\_i the country mean and u from the country's recentred residuals; ε = 0.48. C: design of the earlier version of this table (random walk in ln W from the country's first observed year, u from Δln W $-$ ε Δln Y, not recentred), rerun on the same grid of ε. 1,000 replications per ε and design. In each replication the annual regressions of Table 1 (1996--2023, controls of Table 1, country and year fixed effects, Table 1 sample) and the preferred specification (five-year averages, controls in t\_p $-$ 1, country and period fixed effects, preferred-specification sample) are re-estimated with the synthetic series. Cells: mean of the simulated coefficients and, below, their 2.5--97.5 percentiles. Slope: OLS slope of the simulated mean on 1 $-$ ε, with the 2.5--97.5 percentiles of the slope computed replication by replication. Sanity check (registered in the second plan addendum): in A, the slope of the same-year coefficient is negative with an interval that excludes zero, and at ε = 1 the mean is within 10\% of the observed coefficient in absolute value with an interval that contains zero; the anchored design passes it. Within-country SD, AR(1) (pooled OLS on the lag) and correlation with the placebo ratio: means over replications, Table 1 sample. D: the same-year ratio replaced by its three log components ($\times$100), estimated jointly; covariance and correlation of the numerator innovation with growth after removing country and year effects; regressions of 100 $\times$ Δln W on real growth, with country and year fixed effects; Driscoll-Kraay standard errors (maximum lag 3). The coefficient on nominal GDP growth in D is mechanically positive because real growth, the dependent variable, is part of nominal growth. Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the second plan addendum).\end{minipage}
\end{table}

Panel G: simulated mean of the same-year coefficient over the observed one ($-$0.723), by design; the placebo row is the coefficient of the fixed-numerator placebo ratio over the observed one.
